title: DC-area forecast: Showers stick around this weekend, then nice fall weather ahead
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Widespread showers increasingly focus on the southern half of the region by late morning into the afternoon, with highs in the 60s.

What’s next? Some more light rain is possible Sunday morning into at least part of the afternoon. It’s followed by crisp and sunny fall weather next week.

Today’s daily digit — 6/10: Not exactly the nice fall weather we would like to start the weekend, but some areas should see showers wane by afternoon. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

Forecast in detail

Today (Saturday): Showers across the area this morning should increasingly focus on the southern half of the region into the afternoon. Totals range from about 0.1 to 0.25 inches in the northern suburbs to around 0.5 inches, with some 1-inch tallies, in Southern Maryland. Skies remain largely cloudy, though there could be a few breaks, especially north of the Beltway. Highs are in the 60s. Winds remain light from the north at around 5 to 10 mph. Confidence: Medium

Radar forecast for today

Tonight: There could be a random shower around during the evening, but a mostly dry night is expected before more widespread showers return around predawn or toward sunrise. Overnight lows in the upper 50s to low 60s. Confidence: Medium

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Sunday): Overcast skies are likely, with periods of steadier light rain possible from the morning through mid- to late afternoon. New rainfall totals could reach around 0.2 to 0.4 inches south and east of DC, while areas north and west may see very little to about 0.1 inch. Highs range from near 60 to the mid-60s. Confidence: Medium-Low

Tomorrow night: Mostly cloudy skies stick with us as showers move offshore. A few lingering sprinkles are possible, mainly east of DC. Most of the region should stay dry. Lows dip into the upper 50s to low 60s. Confidence: Medium

A look ahead

Clouds may linger into the morning on Monday, but skies should eventually turn mostly sunny, as highs reach the upper 60s to low 70s. It starts to feel more like fall with drier air (dew points in the mid-50s). Winds turn a bit breezy from the northwest, around 10 to 15 mph with occasional higher gusts. Monday night lows cool down into the 40s. Confidence: Medium

Plenty of sunshine and that fall feel continue through midweek. Highs reach the low to mid-60s on Tuesday before climbing to the mid- to upper 60s on Wednesday. Light winds around 5 to 10 mph both days. Overnight lows mainly in the 40s, with some 30s possible in typical cold spots north and west. Confidence: Medium-High

DC weather history for October 3

A torrential 1927 storm ended a late-season heat wave, dumping record rain and unleashing damaging winds that flooded streets and disrupted services across the city.
